priority.title: Priority and queue ordering
priority.intro: Define priority classes, choose how each service group orders its queue, and check the result in a dry run before it affects anyone.
priority.classes.title: Priority classes
priority.classes.intro: A class gives its tickets a head start: minutes of waiting they are credited on arrival. Normal is 0. A ticket that waits longer than its class's maximum is escalated and served before every ticket that is not.
priority.classes.defaultNote: The default class always has a head start of 0 and cannot be deactivated. Give it a maximum wait to protect ordinary tickets from waiting too long.
priority.classes.summary: Head start: {headstart} min · Maximum wait: {maxWait} · Prefix: {prefix}
priority.classes.confirmDeactivate: {name} will no longer be offered when a ticket is issued. Tickets that already have it keep it.
priority.strategy.title: Ordering strategy
priority.strategy.intro: Each service group orders the tickets waiting for its services in one of these ways. A change applies the next time the queue is read; no waiting ticket is changed.
priority.strategy.weighted_wait: Weighted wait: wait + head start + bonuses
priority.strategy.strict_priority: Strict priority: class first, then first come first served
priority.strategy.fifo: First come first served: creation order only
priority.strategy.default: Not chosen yet: weighted wait is used.
priority.strategy.saved: Saved. The queue follows this strategy from its next read; no waiting ticket was changed.
priority.dryRun.title: Dry run
priority.dryRun.intro: See how every waiting ticket of a service is scored and ordered, without calling anyone.
priority.dryRun.empty: Nobody is waiting for this service.
priority.dryRun.note: Only weighted wait orders by score. The other strategies show the same terms but order as described above. An escalation bonus is very large on purpose: it puts an escalated ticket before every ticket that is not.
